intro.heading: Where am I on the journey?
intro.description: Faith and spiritual life rarely move in a straight line — they unfold in a spiral we travel, revisit, and deepen over a lifetime. This is a gentle mirror, not a test. Eleven honest questions, about five minutes.
intro.meta: No right answers · No email required to see your result
intro.inclusion_note: Homeward is rooted in Jesus, but you do not need settled beliefs, church experience, or traditional language for God to take this reflection. Answer from where you honestly are today.

stages.title: Inherited Faith
stages.description: You're carrying a spiritual or faith framework that was largely handed to you — by family, church, a recovery community, or culture. There can be real gift in that inheritance: roots, belonging, and a sense of the sacred. Right now it may feel settled and mostly unquestioned, and that's a genuine place to stand. Homeward isn't here to shake it loose. It's here to help what you have received become deeply and personally yours.
stages.resonate: You might resonate with: honoring where you came from while staying open to what may deepen next.

stages.title: Honest Questions
stages.tag: The cracks that let the light in
stages.description: Questions have arrived that you can't un-ask. Maybe old answers stopped fitting, your language for God has changed, or something happened that a tidy spiritual framework couldn't hold. This can feel lonely, but questioning is not a failure of faith or honesty. It may be a sign that you are refusing to settle for something too small. Homeward makes room for doubt, uncertainty, and the questions you are still learning to name.
stages.resonate: You might resonate with: questions born of honesty and longing — questions that may lead toward a larger, more lived spiritual life.

stages.title: Sacred Search
stages.description: You're actively looking — reading, reflecting, praying differently, or exploring practices and voices you weren't handed. You may be searching for God, a Higher Power, meaning, or simply a spiritual life that feels honest and alive. Homeward offers a place to search with others, grounded in the life and way of Jesus and the deep well of contemplative practice, without requiring you to pretend certainty you do not have.
stages.resonate: You might resonate with: contemplative practice, honest community, and teachers who take both spiritual hunger and hard questions seriously.

stages.title: New Foundations
stages.description: You've been through some unmaking and are rebuilding a spiritual life or faith that is simpler in some ways, deeper in others, and unmistakably your own. It can hold mystery without needing to control it and conviction without pretending certainty. What this season needs is community that can match its depth and keep it from drifting into isolation. That's the kind of table Homeward is setting, rooted in Jesus and spacious enough for honest questions.
stages.resonate: You might resonate with: depth over certainty, practice over performance, and companions for the long road.

stages.title: Embodied Faith
stages.tag: Letting faith become a way of life
stages.description: Faith or spirituality is becoming more than a set of beliefs for you — it is becoming a whole-person way of being. Prayer, presence, compassion, justice, and love are becoming the texture of ordinary days. You may find yourself wanting to help others discover this kind of grounded life too. Homeward would love to walk with you and, quite possibly, invite you to help shape and lead.
stages.resonate: You might resonate with: a rule of life, spiritual practice, and helping build something real for others.

stages.title: Living Awake
stages.description: You've come round the spiral to a kind of second simplicity — awake to God or the sacred in ordinary life, able to hold paradox with peace, and drawn to pour love outward. Whether your language is traditional or still evolving, this isn't an arrival; it is a way of continuing to journey while helping carry others home. If you sense a call to help form and lead a Jesus-centered community like this, we'd genuinely love to talk.
stages.resonate: You might resonate with: contemplation in action, mentoring others, and co-creating community.

questions.question: Which feels most true about your spiritual life right now?
questions.hint: Choose the one that fits best today — even if none fits perfectly.
options: The spiritual or faith framework I inherited still fits — I feel settled and at peace.
I still have some form of faith or trust, but I'm carrying real questions I can't shake.
I'm searching — exploring God, a Higher Power, meaning, or what I actually believe.
I've been rebuilding my spiritual life into something more honest and my own.
Faith or spirituality has become a whole way of living for me, not just a set of beliefs.
I feel deeply grounded in God, a Higher Power, or the sacred — and I want to help others find that depth.

questions.question: Have you ever gone through a season of deeply wrestling with what you believe — or whether you believe at all?
questions.hint: There's no better answer here — steadiness, struggle, and uncertainty can all be honest places to be.
options: Yes — deeply.
A little, here and there.
Not really — my beliefs or outlook have felt fairly steady.

questions.question: When questions, doubts, or uncertainty arise, where do they usually lead you?
options: Deeper — they've expanded my faith or spiritual life.
Into rebuilding — I'm putting something more honest together.
Into searching — I've stepped back and I'm still looking.
Further away from organized faith or spirituality for now.
They don't come up much — I'm mostly content where I am.

questions.question: What has your experience with church or organized religion been?
options: I'm involved, and it feels like home.
I'm involved, but something feels off.
I used to be involved and have stepped back, but I'm still open.
I've intentionally stayed away or left.
Church or organized religion has never really been part of my life.

questions.question: When it comes to Jesus, God, a Higher Power, and other spiritual paths, which comes closest to what you believe?
questions.hint: Answer honestly — questions are welcome here, and there's no “right” answer to score.
options: Jesus is the one way to God.
Jesus is my primary path, while I trust others may encounter God or the sacred differently.
I believe many spiritual paths hold real truth about God, a Higher Power, or the sacred.
I'm still working out what — if anything — I believe about God, a Higher Power, or the sacred.

questions.question: How do you relate to contemplative practice?
questions.hint: Contemplative practice includes silence, stillness, breath, visualization, prayer, and reflective awareness. People use these practices to become more present to God, a Higher Power, the sacred, or simply life as it is.
options: It's new to me — I haven't really explored it.
I'm curious, and I'd like to learn.
I practice it now and then.
It's becoming central to how I live.

questions.question: Which sounds most like you?
options: I find real peace in clear beliefs and a spiritual framework I can stand on.
I'm learning to be at peace with questions and mystery.
I care more about growing than about being right.
I can hold deep conviction and real openness at the same time.

questions.question: What are you most longing for in this season of life?
options: A place to truly belong
To grow spiritually
Room for honest questions
A deeper connection with God, a Higher Power, or the sacred
Meaning and purpose
Real friendships with people who value depth and honesty

questions.question: Where are you, and how might you connect — if you ever wanted to?
questions.hint: This isn't asking whether you're interested — only what would fit your life. The next question covers interest.
options: Fort Worth area — I'd be open to meeting in person
Fort Worth area — online would suit me better
Outside the Fort Worth area — online would work best
Not sure / just here to reflect

questions.question: Is there anything you'd like from Homeward?
questions.hint: No pressure at all — this just helps us know how to care for you.
options: I'd love to explore joining a Circle
I'd try something online
Just keep me posted for now
I might want to help build this
Nothing right now — thank you
